name: ViTMatte (base)
purpose: Stray hairs on the edges of Subject, Background and People masks.

data: Composition-1k (from Adobe's Deep Image Matting dataset, distributed on request for research)

notes: Converted by research/prototypes/masking/convert_vitmatte.py (ViTMatte-base, fixed 1024x1024 tiles; the backbone's position embeddings frozen for that size) and compress_vitmatte.py (8-bit weights in blocks of 32; within 0.002 of fp16 on average over a portrait tile's unsure pixels). On hair_bench's heads, over a band from 1% of the long side inside the coarse edge to 5% outside, it halves closed-form matting's error along the edge and keeps 43% of the strands against 15% (vitmatte_bench.py). 0.2 s a tile on an M1 Ultra's GPU; the Neural Engine is slower. Its training data allows research use only; the owner accepted it for everyone as an exception (DEC-35). Version 2 (MSK-33) is version 1 with the 24 relative-position tables that global and windowed attention's matmuls take as constants back in float16 (decompress_vitmatte.py; 111.1 MB against 108.8): on macOS 27.0.1 Metal Performance Shaders Graph aborted in 28 of 1,296 fresh loads of version 1 on the GPU (vitmatte_gpu_probe.py), rebuilding such a matmul with another table's shape, and in none of 850 of version 2; on the GPU its Subject and People masks are version 1's bit for bit, on macOS 26 and 27. Published, with the owner's approval (DEC-26), as the prerelease models-vitmatte-base-v2, with its licence (LICENSE.txt); version 1 stays as models-vitmatte-base-v1. On its own, on the evaluation set's photos it pulls background beside the subject into the matte (dark, flat or foliage backgrounds); the app adds to closed-form matting's matte only the strands it finds (ViTMatte.strands), which adds over a quarter of coverage on at most 0.07% of a frame, mostly hair (vitmatte_bench.py eval --folder eval-strands-app), so it is cleared for everyone again.
